analysis.title: US Equity Rotation / German Factory Orders / France Industrial Production / BoE To Hike
key_insights: US tech stocks lag a post-midterm bounce as momentum and semiconductors unwind and investors rotate toward quality and defensive growth. The debate is whether hyperscalers pull development spend forward ahead of tighter regulation, which could lift 2027 spend but bring an earlier rollover in semis EPS revisions.

Flows favour hyperscalers over neoclouds, possibly reflecting scarcity value of existing compute capacity if scrutiny of new builds rises. The cash desk is a better buyer of hyperscalers and semi-cap equipment and better for sale in memory.

Selective buying in Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Lam Research. Intel, ServiceNow, CoreWeave, Advanced Micro Devices and Sandisk are better for sale. UBXXVOLT (AI Power) fell to a 52-week low on Texas regulatory and execution risk.

Brent fell to $93.22/bbl on Wednesday, lowest since late August, then recovered to about $95.70/bbl Thursday. Lower oil and expectations that a Democratic Congress constrains fiscal expansion pushed the 10-year yield down as much as 10bp, and the DXY lower.

Some excess positioning in semis and AI is clearing and Wednesday's washout may be close to pricing the bad news. Friday's nonfarm payrolls is the main remaining macro catalyst this week, then attention returns to earnings.

German September factory orders rose 4.4% m/m vs 4.5% consensus, after a revised 10.1% August decline. German October final manufacturing PMI was 54.2, but September retail sales fell 2.0% m/m vs a 0.4% rise expected.

France September industrial production fell 0.5% m/m vs a 0.3% rise expected, and 1.3% y/y vs a 0.3% fall expected. Q3 GDP contracted 0.1%, October flash composite PMI was 48.4, and strikes and a deadlocked 2026 budget add political pressure.

UBS economist Anna Titareva expects the BoE to hike 25bp to 4.0% Thursday, in line with consensus, with a 7-2 vote (Dhingra and Taylor on hold). She expects a pause in December and a final 25bp hike in February to 4.25%, more dovish than market pricing.

Sweden October CPI undershot (headline 0.9% y/y vs 1.2%, CPIF 1.1% vs 1.4%) a day after the Riksbank hiked 25bp to 2%. Market prices 2bp for December, 18bp for February, 21.5bp for March and 20bp for May. The desk finds the May meeting interesting.
Norges Bank held at 4.50% as expected and kept a higher-for-longer stance with a hiking bias. New forecasts come in December and the market prices no move for a year.

Australia October composite PMI fell to 47.7 from 50.8 while output prices rose to 56.9. UBS's George Tharenou expects the RBA to hold at 4.85% for a prolonged period. Deputy governor Hauser stayed hawkish.
BoJ September minutes point to further hikes, with one member favouring a faster pace if inflation overshoots. The policy rate is 1.25% and markets expect a December hike.

Banxico is expected by UBS's Rafael De La Fuente to cut 25bp to 6.25% Thursday although only 5 of 30 economists expect a cut. Brazil's Copom held Selic at 13.75% with a hawkish tone, raised its 2027 inflation forecast to 4.7% from 3.9%, and dropped its easing-cycle guidance.

US equity positioning turned more supportive Wednesday: five CTA buy triggers crossed and SPX dealer gamma turned positive after three negative days. SPY rallied 1.7% with $60bn of S&P 500 excess buying, mostly in the first 45 minutes, and an estimated $25-35bn of risk-control selling remains for Thursday.

FX desk prefers short EURGBP over GBPUSD for GBP strength. Cable broke the 200dma at 1.3423 and tested 1.3500 twice, with 1.3550 next on a break. Gold holds above 4,105 and the desk prefers long silver toward 53.25 with a buy zone near 52.00/10.

Rheinmetall fell 13% after missing Q3 and cutting full-year sales and margin guidance for the second time this year, on Boxer and Arminius procurement delays pushing orders into 2027. The UBS EU Defence basket fell 4.61% as defence names sold off after the Democratic sweep of Congress.

vol_and_positioning: Five CTA buy triggers were crossed Wednesday and SPX dealer gamma turned positive after three days negative.

SPY rose 1.7% with $60bn of S&P 500 excess buying, almost all in the first 45 minutes. After 10:15am, S&P excess buying slowed to $2bn and Nasdaq saw $17bn of excess selling, and retail market making clients sold the rally.
An estimated $15-20bn of Wednesday's $40-55bn risk-control sell rebalance is done, leaving $25-35bn of residual selling on Thursday.
Momentum and semiconductors saw a sharp unwind, and some excess positioning in semis and AI looks to be clearing.
Gold buying is driven by fast money rather than real money, and silver short positioning supports the desk's long preference.
geopolitical: US midterm elections produced a Democratic sweep of Congress, read as constraining fiscal expansion and US military spending.
Possible tighter regulation of hyperscalers and Texas AI power scrutiny after the midterms.
Ongoing war in Iran and Middle East conflict keep energy-driven inflation risk elevated.
Iran remains unwilling to relinquish nuclear and Strait of Hormuz objectives, limiting the scope for a European bond rally.
Nationwide strikes and protests in France over the cost of living, with the 2026 budget deadlocked in parliament.
